chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the man who marries the woman without witnesses, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the marriage of the couple regarding what is between him and Allah. The witnesses were made (necessary) in the marriage of the couple only for the sake of the children. Had it not been for that, there would not be a problem with it.'
ai.seo_question: Is a marriage valid without witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the absence of witnesses does not invalidate the marriage contract (*nikah*) itself, as the core agreement stands between the spouses and God. He explains that the primary jurisprudential purpose of requiring witnesses is pragmatic—specifically to establish lineage (*nasab*) and prevent disputes over children—rather than being an intrinsic pillar of the contract's validity. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between the essential elements of marriage and the evidentiary requirements for public recognition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara Bin Ayn who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who married the woman without witnesses. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with a marriage at all regarding what is between him and Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. But rather, the witnesses have been made (necessary) regarding the marriage due to the reason of the children. Had it not been that, there would not be a problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who married a woman without witness. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful at all between him and Allah. Witness in marriage is for the sake of children, if that is not the concern then it is not unlawful.’”
